title: Stronglad
safeHtml:
'''Stronglad''' is one of the Sub-Districts of Asylum. It is located at the Central South Area of Asylum, and its District Code is 29-10.

History

There has been two possible sources regarding the name of Exalt Gardens. One of them has to do with paying homage to Winky Wong, a former member of the Hong Kong-based Beanies, and the other was the fact that an expedition team headed for Coopol passed by this area and saw many strong lads.

Stronglad was previously divided into Stronglad West and Stronglad East. While Stronglad West became Stronglad, Stronglad East became Hawynveil.

Despite being one of the areas with a significant public housing presence, this District also houses the second largest Private Housing Project in Asylum in the name of Wonder Central. Wonder Central Phase 1 features a Shopping Mall, and is one of the few Housing Estates with its own Interior Shopping Mall. With a size smaller than only Seaside Broadwalk, Wonder Central features a total of 4808 flats, with each flat featuring triple rooms.

Future Development

The West Side of Stronglad will be majorly developed in conjunction with Snowty, and had therefore seen possibility of increasing housing. However, the type of housing that will be built is unknown.

Station Characteristics

  • This station is one of the Group 2 Gateways of Nazca Railway, and is located at approximately 20 km to the southwest of Metropolis Terminal.The other three stations in the same group are , and .</ref>
  • This station is the permanent upbound terminus of .
  • This station broke the record of Sand Martin Checkpoint, Apple Hill Station and Fall Point Gateway as the station with the third most number of platforms at 16 platforms, behind Metropolis Terminal and Centopia. However, only 12 of the 16 platforms are used by Nazca Railway.

Fun Facts

  • The platforms of this station are Bay Platforms.
  • The in-station transit of this station is a circular line that runs only in the clockwise direction. The order of the stations are East Concourse Station, West Concourse Station and Shops Station. In fact, this is the first instance of a circular in-station transit in Nazca Railway.
  • All Group 2 Gateways make use of a shape at the sides of its walls. This Station uses Quadrilaterals.

Future Development

  • According to the Nazca Railway 2021 Development Outline, this station will become the permanent upbound terminus of that already interchanges with at Diamond Pool Station in the other end.
  • According to the Nazca Railway Development Plan 2024 Edition, and will connect to this station.

It stretches from Purplaetus at the south, branches out to the east in the name of Tai Lok Street at Tai Hing Estate, and connects to Tai Hing Road Extension as it continues to Bondhill Curves.

'''Tai Hing Elevated''' is an elevated roadway locating above Tai Hing Road, and it spans from Gampton Estate, passing above Shek Pai Tau East Roundabout, through Leung Tin Elevated as an interchange, providing an exit to Tsit Kok Street, and ends in direct connection to Sai Toi Shan Road towards Pak Sheung Street.

As a physical boundary dividing two major development areas of Dansein and Tin Kum-Shek Pai Tau New Town, Tai Hing Road kept layering more structures over time. It also witnessed the long history of development in the two areas, spanning over generations of developers, and the entirety of the Tin-Shek New Town redevelopment.

History

Tai Hing Road was constructed and opened as a four-lane dual carriageway at the east fringe of the Shek Pai Tau New Town, very soon after the Town was founded. Developers of the adjacent Dansein Residential Area flattened the land east of the road immediately after, in reserve for expansion of future housing developments. This results in Tai Hing Road diving up the two development areas as a major arterial, showing a difference in development styles and progresses on both sides of the road. Following south the road connects to Purplaetus and other areas of Peckern, while the north curves perpendicularly to Constellation Circuit (Tai Lok Street in present) at the east.

Later when the same developers at Dansein took over Shek Pai Tau and rebranded as Tin Shek New Town, reconstructions began at the Shek Pai Tau side to unify the building styles. Large-scale expansion and projects were also done on Tai Hing Road, including turning a signal-controlled intersection into a semi-spiral roundabout, constructing Tai Hing Elevated and SLT tracks, etc. However because of land constraints, the structures on Tai Hing Road became more and more complex than before, with sections containing 5 layers of roadway and railway strcutres.

In spite of relocating Tai Hing Estate to the north, and the development of Dansein North Residential area, Tai Hing Road was extended northward in a separate name as Tai Hing Road Extension to Southouse Centre (the extension was renamed Nottingham Road past Fai Ming Estate). Meanwhile during the construction of Po Tin Street Interim Housing, the curve and the segment to the east were reconstructed as a semi-spiral roundabout with adjustments to the roadway volume, and later renamed as Tai Lok Street.

Current Status

Tai Hing Road currently carries traffic coming from Dansein Market and Dansein North, with its elevated overpasses, underground railway tracks, sandwiching SLT tracks, and bus stops on both sides. The spatially-constrained roadway passes through the Uk Hip region, and evolves into ramps with Route 12 on the way to Purplaetus, as one of the main arterials supporting the urbanized region of Peckern North.
